definition.handoff: parent exports the 18-key table under policy verifier:v1; a separate process imports it under its own policy, reads, attempts one unlisted-authority correction, applies one allowed-authority correction, and exports; parent imports the child export
definition.child_read: child must read the 20 describe sentences at 40/40 and the zero lines at 0/0
definition.child_policy: child policy is verifier:v1; a correction from verifier:v2 must be rejected_batch_unknown_authority, then verifier:v1 must be accepted
definition.digest_chain: child imported digest equals parent digest; child exported digest equals parent-imported digest after the handback
definition.corrupt_child: a second child receives truncated bytes and must reject them with a ValueError whose message starts with rejected_import_invalid_state; it must not write an output table
definition.closed_state: the nine closed-state readings stay equal before and after

criteria.child_import: child imported digest equals the parent digest
criteria.child_policy: unlisted authority rejected as rejected_batch_unknown_authority; allowed authority accepted with one log entry
criteria.handback: parent import of the child export has the same digest as the child export; alias reads RED; log authority is verifier:v1 and reason is child:accepted; 40/40 and 0/0
criteria.corrupt_child: child result carries an error starting with rejected_import_invalid_state and no output bytes
criteria.closed_state: the nine closed-state readings stay equal before and after
criteria.reporting: the child runs in a separate Python process; the report records its return code and the sha256 of both state files, so the handoff is not an in-process object copy
